goal.sl: Ločiš pridevnik od prislova, pišeš quickly, carefully, happily in gently, rečeš well, fast, hard, postaviš prislov za predmet in poveš faster, better, more slowly.
goal.de: Du unterscheidest Adjektiv und Adverb, schreibst quickly, carefully, happily und gently, sagst well, fast, hard, stellst das Adverb nach das Objekt und sagst faster, better, more slowly.
goal.it: Distingui aggettivo e avverbio, scrivi quickly, carefully, happily e gently, dici well, fast, hard, metti l'avverbio dopo il complemento e dici faster, better, more slowly.
goal.en: You can tell an adjective from an adverb, spell quickly, carefully, happily and gently, say well, fast, hard, put the adverb after the object and say faster, better, more slowly.

say.sl: Pridevnik pove, kakšna je stvar, prislov pa, kako kdo nekaj dela: **a slow walk** (počasen sprehod), a **Jack walks slowly.** (Jack hodi počasi.) **a careful driver** (previden voznik), a **Sam drives carefully.** (Sam vozi previdno.) Ljudje rečejo tudi *Drive careful!*, pisno pa velja **carefully**.
say.de: Ein Adjektiv sagt, wie etwas ist, ein Adverb, wie man etwas tut: **a slow walk** (eine langsame Wanderung), aber **Jack walks slowly.** (Jack geht langsam.) **a careful driver** (ein vorsichtiger Fahrer), aber **Sam drives carefully.** (Sam fährt vorsichtig.) Das Deutsche sagt beides gleich, das Englische nicht. Viele sagen auch *Drive careful!*, geschrieben gilt **carefully**.
say.it: L'aggettivo dice com'è una cosa, l'avverbio come si fa qualcosa: **a slow walk** (una camminata lenta), ma **Jack walks slowly.** (Jack cammina lentamente.) **a careful driver** (un autista prudente), ma **Sam drives carefully.** (Sam guida con prudenza.) Molti dicono anche *Drive careful!*, per iscritto vale **carefully**.
say.en: An adjective says what a thing is like, an adverb how something is done: **a slow walk**, but **Jack walks slowly.** **a careful driver**, but **Sam drives carefully.** People also say *Drive careful!* and *walk slow*; writing wants **carefully**, **slowly**.

examples.en: Jack walks slowly up the fell.
examples.de: Jack geht langsam den Berg hinauf.

say.sl: Večina dobi **-ly**: **quick, quickly** (hiter, hitro); **quiet, quietly** (tih, tiho). **-ful** obdrži oba l: **careful, carefully** (previden, previdno). Soglasnik + **-y** postane **-ily**: **happy, happily** (srečen, srečno); **easy, easily** (lahek, zlahka). Končni **-le** postane **-ly**: **gentle, gently** (nežen, nežno); **terrible, terribly** (grozen, grozno).
say.de: Die meisten bekommen **-ly**: **quick, quickly** (schnell); **quiet, quietly** (leise). **-ful** behält beide l: **careful, carefully** (vorsichtig). Konsonant + **-y** wird zu **-ily**: **happy, happily** (glücklich); **easy, easily** (leicht). Ein **-le** am Ende wird zu **-ly**: **gentle, gently** (sanft); **terrible, terribly** (schrecklich).
say.it: La maggior parte prende **-ly**: **quick, quickly** (veloce, velocemente); **quiet, quietly** (silenzioso, in silenzio). **-ful** tiene le due l: **careful, carefully** (prudente, con prudenza). Consonante + **-y** diventa **-ily**: **happy, happily** (felice, felicemente); **easy, easily** (facile, facilmente). Una **-le** finale diventa **-ly**: **gentle, gently** (delicato, delicatamente); **terrible, terribly** (terribile, terribilmente).
say.en: Most take **-ly**: **quick, quickly**; **quiet, quietly**. **-ful** keeps both l's: **careful, carefully** (never *carefuly*). A consonant + **-y** becomes **-ily**: **happy, happily** (never *happyly*); **easy, easily**. A final **-le** becomes **-ly**: **gentle, gently**; **terrible, terribly**.

say.sl: **good** postane **well** (dobro): **Granny Maggie sings well.** (Babica Maggie dobro poje.) Ljudje rečejo tudi *sings good*, pisno pa velja **well**. **fast**, **hard**, **late** in **early** se ne spremenijo: **Meg runs fast.** (Meg hitro teče.), nikoli *fastly*. **Mrs Birkett works hard.** (Gospa Birkett trdo dela.) **hardly** (komaj) in **lately** (zadnje čase) sta drugi besedi.
say.de: **good** wird zu **well** (gut): **Granny Maggie sings well.** (Oma Maggie singt gut.) Viele sagen auch *sings good*, geschrieben gilt **well**. **fast**, **hard**, **late** und **early** bleiben gleich: **Meg runs fast.** (Meg läuft schnell.), nie *fastly*. **Mrs Birkett works hard.** (Frau Birkett arbeitet hart.) **hardly** (kaum) und **lately** (in letzter Zeit) sind andere Wörter.
say.it: **good** diventa **well** (bene): **Granny Maggie sings well.** (Nonna Maggie canta bene.) Molti dicono anche *sings good*, per iscritto vale **well**. **fast**, **hard**, **late** e **early** non cambiano: **Meg runs fast.** (Meg corre veloce.), mai *fastly*. **Mrs Birkett works hard.** (La signora Birkett lavora sodo.) **hardly** (appena) e **lately** (ultimamente) sono altre parole.
say.en: **good** becomes **well**: **Granny Maggie sings well.** People also say *sings good*; writing wants **well**. **fast**, **hard**, **late** and **early** don't change: **Meg runs fast.** (never *Meg runs fastly.*) **Mrs Birkett works hard.** **hardly** (almost not) and **lately** (recently) are other words.

say.sl: Prislov gre za glagol, in za predmet, če ga glagol ima: **Sam plays darts well.** (Sam dobro igra pikado.), nikoli *Sam plays well darts.* **Jack closed the gate quietly.** (Jack je tiho zaprl vrata.) Prislov na **-ly** lahko stoji tudi pred glagolom: **Jack quietly closed the gate.** Nikoli med glagolom in predmetom.
say.de: Das Adverb steht nach dem Verb, und nach dem Objekt, wenn es eins hat: **Sam plays darts well.** (Sam spielt gut Darts.), nie *Sam plays well darts.* **Jack closed the gate quietly.** (Jack schloss leise das Gatter.) Ein Adverb auf **-ly** kann auch vor dem Verb stehen: **Jack quietly closed the gate.** Nie zwischen Verb und Objekt.
say.it: L'avverbio va dopo il verbo, e dopo il complemento se c'è: **Sam plays darts well.** (Sam gioca bene a freccette.), mai *Sam plays well darts.* **Jack closed the gate quietly.** (Jack ha chiuso piano il cancello.) Un avverbio in **-ly** può stare anche prima del verbo: **Jack quietly closed the gate.** Mai tra il verbo e il complemento.
say.en: The adverb goes after the verb, and after its object if it has one: **Sam plays darts well.** (never *Sam plays well darts.*) **Jack closed the gate quietly.** A **-ly** adverb can also stand before the verb: **Jack quietly closed the gate.** Never between the verb and its object.

examples.it: Jack ha chiuso piano il cancello.
La signora Hartley parla inglese chiaramente.

say.sl: Za **be**, **look**, **feel**, **smell** in **taste** pride pridevnik, saj povedo, kakšna je stvar: **The soup smells good.** (Juha dobro diši.) **You look tired.** (Videti si utrujen{m:|f:a}.) **Jack is careful.** (Jack je previden.) A **Jack works carefully.** (Jack dela previdno.) **friendly** (prijazen) in **lovely** (ljubek) se končata na **-ly**, a sta pridevnika: **a friendly dog**.
say.de: Nach **be**, **look**, **feel**, **smell** und **taste** kommt ein Adjektiv, denn sie sagen, wie etwas ist: **The soup smells good.** (Die Suppe riecht gut.) **You look tired.** (Du siehst müde aus.) **Jack is careful.** (Jack ist vorsichtig.) Aber **Jack works carefully.** (Jack arbeitet vorsichtig.) **friendly** (freundlich) und **lovely** (reizend) enden auf **-ly**, sind aber Adjektive: **a friendly dog**.
say.it: Dopo **be**, **look**, **feel**, **smell** e **taste** viene un aggettivo, perché dicono com'è una cosa: **The soup smells good.** (La zuppa ha un buon profumo.) **You look tired.** (Sembri stanc{m:o|f:a}.) **Jack is careful.** (Jack è prudente.) Ma **Jack works carefully.** (Jack lavora con attenzione.) **friendly** (gentile) e **lovely** (adorabile) finiscono in **-ly**, ma sono aggettivi: **a friendly dog**.
say.en: After **be**, **look**, **feel**, **smell** and **taste** comes an adjective, as they say what a thing is like: **The soup smells good.** **You look tired.** **Jack is careful.** But **Jack works carefully.** **friendly** and **lovely** end in **-ly** but are adjectives: **a friendly dog**.

examples.it: La zuppa ha un buon profumo.

say.sl: Ko primerjaš, kako kdo kaj dela: **fast, faster** (hitreje); **hard, harder** (bolj trdo); **well, better** (bolje); **badly, worse** (slabše). Prislov na **-ly** dobi **more**: **slowly, more slowly** (počasneje). **Can you speak more slowly, please?** (Lahko govorite počasneje, prosim?) V govoru slišiš tudi **slower** in **louder**.
say.de: Zum Vergleichen, wie man etwas tut: **fast, faster** (schneller); **hard, harder** (härter); **well, better** (besser); **badly, worse** (schlechter). Ein Adverb auf **-ly** bekommt **more**: **slowly, more slowly** (langsamer). **Can you speak more slowly, please?** (Können Sie bitte langsamer sprechen?) Gesprochen hörst du auch **slower** und **louder**.
say.it: Per confrontare come si fa qualcosa: **fast, faster** (più veloce); **hard, harder** (più sodo); **well, better** (meglio); **badly, worse** (peggio). Un avverbio in **-ly** prende **more**: **slowly, more slowly** (più lentamente). **Can you speak more slowly, please?** (Può parlare più lentamente, per favore?) A voce senti anche **slower** e **louder**.
say.en: To compare what is done: **fast, faster**; **hard, harder**; **well, better**; **badly, worse**. A **-ly** adverb takes **more**: **slowly, more slowly**. **Can you speak more slowly, please?** In speech you also hear **slower** and **louder**.

exercises.text: Mr Dixon works ___ (hard) at the smithy. He doesn't talk ___ (quick): he says a few words ___ (slow) and ___ (clear). The horses stand ___ (quiet) while he works ___ (careful). Is he a ___ (good) blacksmith? Yes: he does everything ___ (good)!

translation.sl: Gospod Dixon v kovačnici trdo dela. Ne govori hitro: počasi in razločno reče nekaj besed. Konji mirno stojijo, medtem ko on previdno dela. Je dober kovač? Ja: vse dela dobro!
translation.de: Herr Dixon arbeitet hart in der Schmiede. Er redet nicht schnell: Er sagt langsam und deutlich ein paar Worte. Die Pferde stehen ruhig, während er vorsichtig arbeitet. Ist er ein guter Schmied? Ja: Er macht alles gut!
translation.it: Il signor Dixon lavora sodo alla fucina. Non parla velocemente: dice poche parole, lentamente e chiaramente. I cavalli stanno fermi mentre lui lavora con attenzione. È un bravo fabbro? Sì: fa tutto bene!
translation.en: Mr Dixon works hard at the smithy. He doesn't talk quickly: he says a few words slowly and clearly. The horses stand quietly while he works carefully. Is he a good blacksmith? Yes: he does everything well!
